Read LogPhase600 Excel export

read_logphase_xlsx.Rd

Reads one kind of sheet from an Excel export of a LogPhase600 plate reader. A run can hold up to four 96-well plates, and each plate has its own Results, Raw Data and Procedure sheets (for example Plate 1 - Raw Data). The sheet argument chooses which kind to read; every plate in the file is read and the plates are stacked into one table, identified by plate_id. To keep only some plates, filter on plate_id afterwards.

Usage

read_logphase_xlsx(
  path,
  sheet = c("raw", "results", "procedure"),
  interval_hours = 1/3,
  thin_hours = NULL
)

Arguments

path

Path to the xlsx file.

sheet

Which kind of sheet to read: "raw" (default), "results" or "procedure".

interval_hours, thin_hours

Used only when sheet = "raw". See read_logphase_txt().

Value

A tibble. The columns depend on sheet; all have plate_id, the sheet name without the trailing sheet type (such as "Plate 1").

  • "raw": seconds, hours, well, od and plate_id.

  • "results": one row per well with plate_id, well (zero-padded as for "raw"), lag_hours, max_rate (OD per minute) and stationary_hours. Join to the raw data by plate_id and well.

  • "procedure": one row per plate with plate_id, plate_comment, plate_type, runtime_hours, interval_hours, max_reads, wavelength_nm, incubator, temperature_setpoint_c, temperature_gradient, shaking, shaking_rpm and summary.

Details

  • "raw": the optical density time courses, equivalent to the text files. Processing is the same as for read_logphase_txt().

  • "results": the per-well summary the instrument software computed (lag time, maximum growth rate and stationary phase). These are rarely needed, since the package works from the raw reads, but they are available for comparison with your own estimates. The instrument stores lag time and stationary phase as Excel day fractions, which are converted to hours. Wells for which the software reported no value (????? in the sheet) are NA.

  • "procedure": the run settings recorded for each plate, parsed from the procedure summary text into one row per plate. Times are converted to hours and on/off settings to logicals. The original text is kept in summary, in case a setting is not covered by the parsed columns.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "logphase600_example.xlsx", package = "plateReadeR")
read_logphase_xlsx(f)
#> # A tibble: 2,304 × 5
#>    seconds hours well     od plate_id
#>      <dbl> <dbl> <chr> <dbl> <chr>   
#>  1       0 0     A01   0.116 Plate 1 
#>  2    1200 0.333 A01   0.116 Plate 1 
#>  3    2400 0.667 A01   0.116 Plate 1 
#>  4    3600 1     A01   0.117 Plate 1 
#>  5    4800 1.33  A01   0.117 Plate 1 
#>  6    6000 1.67  A01   0.118 Plate 1 
#>  7    7200 2     A01   0.119 Plate 1 
#>  8    8400 2.33  A01   0.119 Plate 1 
#>  9    9600 2.67  A01   0.119 Plate 1 
#> 10   10800 3     A01   0.119 Plate 1 
#> # ℹ 2,294 more rows
read_logphase_xlsx(f, sheet = "results")
#> # A tibble: 192 × 5
#>    plate_id well  lag_hours    max_rate stationary_hours
#>    <chr>    <chr>     <dbl>       <dbl>            <dbl>
#>  1 Plate 1  A01       NA     0.0000191              4.72
#>  2 Plate 1  B01        4.60  0.00000241             4.69
#>  3 Plate 1  C01       30.1  -0.00000155            37.4 
#>  4 Plate 1  D01       22.5  -0.00000164            27.4 
#>  5 Plate 1  E01       NA    -0.00000270             2.33
#>  6 Plate 1  F01        7.42  0.00000121            11.7 
#>  7 Plate 1  G01       22.9  -0.00000177            28.2 
#>  8 Plate 1  H01       34.6  -0.00000357            35.2 
#>  9 Plate 1  A02        8.82  0.00000162             8.62
#> 10 Plate 1  B02       11.4   0.00000141             5.40
#> # ℹ 182 more rows
read_logphase_xlsx(f, sheet = "procedure")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   plate_id plate_comment plate_type       runtime_hours interval_hours max_reads

#> 1 Plate 1  NA            Corning 96 well…            48          0.333       145
#> 2 Plate 2  NA            Corning 96 well…            48          0.333       145
